original_text: –Illumination Source–The type and source of electromagnetic radiation that is used to illuminate the sample–Light Microscope (LM)–White light generated by LED bulb (tungsten filament light bulb in older microscopes)–Electron Microscopes (EM)–Use beam of focused electrons, usually from a crystal or filament
explanation: This slide defines the illumination source in microscopy, which is the type and source of electromagnetic radiation used to illuminate the sample. It compares two types: 1) Light Microscopes (LM), which use white light generated by an LED bulb (or a tungsten filament light bulb in older models), and 2) Electron Microscopes (EM), which use a beam of focused electrons, typically emitted from a crystal or filament.

questions.q: What is the illumination source in a modern Light Microscope (LM)?
opts: White light generated by an LED bulb
A beam of focused electrons from a crystal

opts: A beam of focused electrons, usually from a crystal or filament
